title: Deployment Safety Lifecycle and Signal Playbook
creator: Anika Sharma
description:
Objective: Create a prescriptive safety lifecycle and signal-driven playbook that coordinates release blockers, abort/rollback decisioning, and templated communications across Product, Engineering, SRE, Design, Legal, and GTM. The playbook will be the canonical runbook used during the runtime-1.22 rollout and referenced in release notes and launch comms.

Scope and deliverables:
- Blocker taxonomy: agreed definitions (P0/P1/P2), examples (data loss, exposed PII, regression in latency beyond 2x baseline, sustained 5xx error rate >1% for 5m), and owner mapping.
- Abort/Abort-to-Rollback criteria: concrete metrics + time windows to trigger a halt (e.g., sustained QPS drop >30% with healthy instances, KV cache invalidation observed, or model output hallucination rate increase detected by eval probe).
- Rollback plan: fast rollback steps for hosted and dedicated deployments, staged rollback variants (soft-fallback to compatible model family, full rollback to prior release, capacity-based throttling), required runbook commands and automation hooks (GitHub PR labels -> CI/CD pipeline rollback job).
- Incident communications templates: internal incident summary, engineering postmortem stub, customer-facing status page updates, partner escalation email, and GTM-safe release note boilerplate. Each template includes placeholders for impact, ETA-to-fix, mitigation steps, and recommended customer guidance.
- Signal catalogue and dashboards: prioritized signals (latency p95, token cost delta, 5xx rate, per-route error rate, KV cache hit ratio, autoscaler saturation), owner for each signal, primary and secondary alert channels, and runbook links.
- Stakeholder roster and escalation ladder: primary owners (SRE, Runtime Eng, API Platform, Product), cross-team liaisons, on-call escalation levels, and executive notification criteria.
- Release-notes and GTM coordination checklist: owners for user-visible changes, review windows, embargo timelines, and legal/marketing sign-offs.
- Automation and enforcement: PR label conventions (release-blocker/rollback-required), preflight CI gates (smoke tests, canary traffic run), and automation tasks for Slack alert attachments and status page templating.

Acceptance criteria:
- Finalized playbook document in Confluence with approval signatures from SRE and Runtime Eng.
- At least three templated communications (internal, customer, status page) reviewed by Legal and GTM.
- CI/CD rollback job created and tested in staging with documented runbook steps.
- Monitoring dashboard with the signal catalogue wired to alerts and ownership assigned.

Risks and mitigations:
- Ownership gaps across teams -> mitigation: weekly pre-launch sync and explicit assignment in playbook.
- Overly broad abort criteria causing false halts -> mitigation: require two corroborating signals before full abort; add canary window extension.
- Communication lag causing customer confusion -> mitigation: automated status page updates and pre-approved GTM templates for immediate posting.

Next steps:
1) Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime Eng, API Platform, Legal, and GTM (target 2026-03-05).
2) Agree on blocker definitions and signal thresholds (deadline 2026-03-10).
3) Prototype rollback automation in staging and run one dry-run (deadline 2026-03-18).
4) Finalize templates and obtain Legal sign-off (deadline 2026-03-22).
5) Publish playbook and add to release notes checklist (deadline 2026-03-25).
